items.title: Protest, suspension, legal battle: What is happening at Kerala’s Sankaracharya University
items.summary: “We are the students of this campus. Not violent protesters,” said Aswanth VM, a Malayalam-language PhD scholar at the Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit (SSUS) in Kalady, Ernakulam. Aswanth is one of three students on an indefinite hunger strike in front of the university. They are demanding the university’s permission to sit for their examinations and for the revocation of suspensions of 16 students. “We will continue our protest until the university agrees to our demand,” Aswanth added. The protest has since spilt over to another campus, the Maharajah’s College in Ernakulam, where SFI students questioned the Education Minister over the issue and were themselves suspended. When TNM visited the university on October 5, the three students, Aswanth, Archana and KV Abhijith – also members of the Students Federation of India (SFI), the student organisation of the Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] – were on the fifth day of their hunger strike. What began as a student protest under SFI on July 22 later escalated into a dispute that reached the Supreme Court of India, with the students seeking a favourable judgement to write their semester examinations. items.title: Tamil Nadu minister accuses DMK of AI-assisted corruption in library book purchases
items.summary: Tamil Nadu School Education Minister Rajmohan has accused the previous Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) government of procuring substandard books from dubious publishers for the Periyar Arivulagam library in Coimbatore. He alleged that the purchases involved the use of artificial intelligence and amounted to corruption. “For the first time in this country, the DMK has engaged in corruption using artificial intelligence,” Rajmohan said at a press conference in Chennai. Displaying a purchase order, the minister said the order for books from Agal Vilakku Publishers was issued on February 14, 2026, when the DMK was in power. The order specified that the books were to be delivered to the Periyar Arivulagam library, he said. Payments to the publishers were released in March 2026. Rajmohan alleged that the previous government had bought books that were fit to be thrown in a dustbin and had them delivered to the library before the Assembly elections in May 2026. He said the boxes were opened only after the elections, ahead of the library's inauguration, and pointed to a June 2026 seal on them as evidence of when they were opened.
